title: Two jobs, one card
lede: Two jobs want more memory than the card has.
why: A free-memory check is a snapshot: two jobs can both pass it, then both load. iris keeps a reservation ledger per card, so it does not grant leases that add up to more than the card, and it checks NVML as well for anything it was not told about.

beats.title: A batch job takes most of the card
beats.text: argus-proof asks for 13.7 GB on the RTX 3090 and gets it at once. This is a reservation: the model has not loaded yet, but nobody else can be promised that memory.

beats.title: The next one does not fit, so it waits
beats.text: argus-forge wants 15.6 GB. Without a broker it would start, and one of the two would likely run out of memory. iris queues it and says why: “waiting for 6966 MB on rtx3090: nothing idle to evict”.

beats.title: A person does not wait behind a training run
beats.text: argus-curator is interactive and fits beside the batch job, so it is granted straight away, ahead of the background job that asked first. Queued jobs gain a class every five minutes, so the training run cannot starve.

beats.title: Released, and the queue moves
beats.text: proof finishes and gives its lease back. Once the agent sees the memory free, forge is granted, 68 seconds after it asked.
